Analogue of SAS PROC MIANALYZE (Rubin pooling)

Source: R/mianalyze.r
ks_mianalyze.Rd

Pools point estimates and standard errors across multiple imputations according to Rubin's rules.

Usage

ks_mianalyze(est, err, alpha = 0.05, theta0 = 0, v0)

mianalyze(est, err, alpha = 0.05, theta0 = 0, v0)

Arguments

est

Numeric vector of point estimates from each imputation.

err

Numeric vector of corresponding standard errors.

alpha

Significance level for confidence intervals. Default \code0.05.

theta0

Null value for hypothesis test \eqnH_0: theta = theta_0.

v0

Optional complete-data degrees of freedom used for Barnard-Rubin style small-sample df adjustment.

Value

An object of class \codeks_mianalyze with components: \describe \itemEstimatePooled estimate. \itemStdErrPooled standard error. \itemmNumber of imputations. \itemVbBetween-imputation variance. \itemVwWithin-imputation variance. \itemVtTotal variance. \itemdfDegrees of freedom. \itemrRelative increase in variance due to nonresponse. \itemlambdaFraction of missing information. \itemreRelative efficiency. \itemlcl, uclTwo-sided confidence limits for \codeEstimate. \itemalphaAlpha used for CI. \itemtheta0Null value used in hypothesis test. \itemminim, maximMin/max of input \codeest. \itemtTest statistic for \eqnH_0. \itempvalTwo-sided p-value.

Details

Let \eqnQ_i and \eqnU_i be estimate and variance from imputation \eqni. The pooled estimate is \eqn\barQ = m^-1\sum_i Q_i; within variance \eqn\barU = m^-1\sum_i U_i; between variance \eqnB = (m-1)^-1\sum_i (Q_i-\barQ)^2; total variance \eqnT = \barU + (1 + 1/m)B.

Degrees of freedom default to Rubin's large-sample expression and can be adjusted using \codev0.

References

Rubin, D. B. (1987). \emphMultiple Imputation for Nonresponse in Surveys. Wiley.

Examples

est <- c(0.345, 0.303, 0.298, 0.378)
err <- c(0.056, 0.101, 0.099, 0.034)
out <- mianalyze(est, err)
out
#> 
#> 
#> ***Variance information (4 Imputations)***
#> Between		Within		Total		DF
#> -------		------		-----		--
#> 0.001426	0.006074	0.007856	58.3
#> 
#> Relative	Fraction
#> Increase	Missing		Relative
#> in Variance	Information	Efficiency
#> -----------	-----------	----------
#> 0.293488	0.252131	0.940705
#> 
#> ***Parameter estimates (4 Imputations)***
#> Estimate	Std Error	95.00% Confidence Limits	DF
#> --------	---------	------------------------	--
#> 0.331000	0.088634	0.153597	0.508403	58.3
#> 
#> 						t for H0
#> Minimum		Maximum		Theta0		Parameter=Theta0	Pr>|t|
#> -------		-------		------		----------------	------
#> 0.298000	0.378000	0.00		3.7345			0.0004

## With finite complete-data df adjustment
mianalyze(est, err, v0 = 120)
#> 
#> 
#> ***Variance information (4 Imputations)***
#> Between		Within		Total		DF
#> -------		------		-----		--
#> 0.001426	0.006074	0.007856	35.6
#> 
#> Relative	Fraction
#> Increase	Missing		Relative
#> in Variance	Information	Efficiency
#> -----------	-----------	----------
#> 0.293488	0.252131	0.940705
#> 
#> ***Parameter estimates (4 Imputations)***
#> Estimate	Std Error	95.00% Confidence Limits	DF
#> --------	---------	------------------------	--
#> 0.331000	0.088634	0.151165	0.510835	35.6
#> 
#> 						t for H0
#> Minimum		Maximum		Theta0		Parameter=Theta0	Pr>|t|
#> -------		-------		------		----------------	------
